item.title: Modeling Iron-Air Battery Arbitrage in U.S. Power Markets
item.description: In recent years, one of the biggest challenges the American grid faces is maintaining reliability and stable power pricing amid massive forecasted load growth. Batteries don’t bring new generation to the grid but can store energy to reduce electricity curtailments, smooth pricing, and increase grid reliability while discharging. Utility-scale lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries have provided a great solution to gas plant ramp rates induced by the end-of-day solar reduction seen in the duck curve, as well as intra-day price smoothing. However, at only four hours of dispatch potential, these batteries are still largely incapable of providing a reliability improvement at times when power demand surges for multiple days at a time, like during a heat dome or prolonged cold front. This gap between market demands and grid infrastructure highlights the opportunity for new technology to be developed and implemented. In this Insight, we investigate the potential use and revenue of iron-air batteries within power markets by assuming a given project would have up to 100 hours of stored energy and roughly a 50% charge-discharge efficiency.

item.title: S&P 500 Earnings Season Update: October 16, 2026
item.description: At this early stage, the third quarter earnings season for the S&P 500 has seen a mixed start relative to expectations. While the percentage of S&P 500 companies reporting positive earnings surprises is above recent averages, the magnitude of earnings surprises is below recent averages. As a result of this mixed performance and downward revisions to EPS estimates for companies in the Health Care sector, the index is reporting lower earnings for the third quarter today relative to the end of last week and relative to the end of the quarter. Despite the decrease in earnings, the index is still reporting (year-over-year) earnings growth above 25% for the 3rd straight quarter.

item.title: Balancing Hyperscale Demand and Ratepayer Protections in Wyoming
item.description: Wyoming’s pitch to hyperscale tech developers has long rested on low-cost industrial power, available rural land, and an agreeable business climate. But as developers announce pipelines exceeding 5 GW of planned hyperscale capacity across the state, which includes multi-gigawatt campuses in Cheyenne, Evanston, and Casper, state regulatory dockets, not site-selection brochures, are defining the economics of deployment. With the Wyoming Public Service Commission (WPSC) reviewing 2026 general rate filings from PacifiCorp d/b/a Rocky Mountain Power (Docket No. 20000-710-ER-26) and Black Hills Power (Docket No. 20002-148-ER-26), the central issue has shifted from site acquisition to cost assignment: who pays for regional generation, high-voltage transmission interconnects, and local substation expansions, and how fast will those expenditures enter the retail rate base?

item.title: From Investment Intent to Portfolio: The Rise of Conversational Portfolio Construction
item.description: Portfolio construction is entering a new phase. Over the past several decades, much of the innovation in portfolio construction has focused on the mathematics: richer objectives, more realistic measures of risk, increasingly sophisticated constraints, transaction costs, taxes, multi-asset class portfolios, and multi-period investment decisions. Those advances have made the underlying machinery much more powerful.

item.title: S&P 500 Likely to Report Earnings Growth Above 35% for Q3
item.description: The current earnings growth rate for the S&P 500 for the third quarter is 29.6%, which would mark the 3rd consecutive quarter of year-over-year earnings growth above 25% for the index. Given that most S&P 500 companies report actual earnings above estimates, what is the likelihood the index will report earnings growth of 29.6% for the quarter?

item.title: Renewable Natural Gas Production Growth in the U.S.
item.description: Utilization of renewable natural gas, or RNG, in the United States has been growing at an increasing rate since 2022. While this growth could be attributed to many factors, the federal incentives provided by the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) in 2022 seem to have provided the optimal environment for RNG to grow rapidly.
